classification.difficultyReason: Restrict reciprocal and linear graphs and interpret a separately defined boundary value.

answer.short: The positive reciprocal branch for $0<x<2$ and the decreasing line for $x>2$ meet at the closed point $(2,\tfrac12)$. The line crosses the $x$-axis at $(4,0)$. The reciprocal approaches the vertical asymptote $x=0$.
answer.worked:
The first subfunction is the positive reciprocal curve; the second is a decreasing straight line.
$$\begin{align*}g(2)&=\frac12,\\h(2)&=1-\frac14(2)=\frac12,\\f(2)&=\frac12.\end{align*}$$
Sketch the reciprocal only for $0<x<2$ and the line only for $x>2$. Although both intervals exclude $2$, the separately specified value fills the point $(2,\tfrac12)$. For the line,
$$\begin{align*}1-\frac14x&=0,\\x&=4.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Positive reciprocal curve joins a descending line at a filled boundary point; guides mark the boundary coordinates.
spec.mathematics: y=1/x on (0,2); y=1-x/4 on (2,infinity); f(2)=1/2; intercept 4.

answer.short: Draw $y=x$ for $x<2$, with the closed point $(2,2)$ supplied by $f(2)=2$. Draw $y=2-x$ for $x>2$ with an open point at $(2,0)$.
answer.worked:
Both subfunctions are straight lines.
$$\begin{align*}g(2)&=2,\\h(2)&=2-2=0,\\f(2)&=2.\end{align*}$$
Sketch $y=x$ to the left of $2$. Its boundary point $(2,2)$ is filled by the separately specified function value. Sketch $y=2-x$ to the right of $2$, leaving $(2,0)$ open.

spec.description: Increasing left line ends at a filled point; decreasing right line starts at a distinct open point.
spec.mathematics: Closed (2,2), open (2,0); left branch y=x, right branch y=2-x.
